=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides, visible in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely packed at the terminal end of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem by a petiole)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins are smooth without teeth, though some minor physical damage is present)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaf is widest below the middle and tapers to a point at both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the tip tapers gradually to a slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaf tapers to a wedge-like shape where it meets the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and clearly visible, spaced relatively evenly along the midrib
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous and shiny (surface appears smooth and reflects light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are visible but relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears brown, firm, and rigid)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent
    19. Stem color: brown (main stem) with green on newer growth
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling shows minor physical damage to the leaf margins (holes and tears) but no clear evidence of herbivory or pathogen. A pink tag is attached to the stem.
